correctness.rationale: Any nonexpansive map of a finite integer interval has consecutive image. Idempotency fixes each image point. Fixing the interval splits the map bijectively into two independent boundary-rooted length-constrained weak-step walks. The r-state lazy-path adjacency matrix enumerates each tail and convolution yields all image-rank counts. Verified r=3 resolvent and five fixed-interval contributions; 131 not 130 at n=7. The packaged direct exhaustive checker enumerates all functions for n=1..7 independently. Boundary n=1, r=1, r=2 and r=n are correctly normalized.

evidence: Zubairu--Ali 2021, Conjecture 14 predicts c_(7,3)=130, while the five independently counted image intervals yield 29+24+25+24+29=131.
Full independent direct enumeration of every map [7]->[7] with idempotency and Lipschitz conditions recovers 131 of rank 3.

originality.rationale: Full text of Zubairu--Ali 2021, especially pp. 239--240, proves selected boundary ranks and explicitly identifies intermediate ranks as open; its Conjecture 14 predicts 130 at n=7 whereas the proved general formula gives 131. Umar--Zubairu 2018 discusses regularity and Green relations, not a complete idempotent image-rank census. Ojo--Al-Kharousi--Umar 2021 studies order-preserving partial contractions. Searches of published results and the literature found no statement implying the all-ranks coefficient formula; unindexed equivalent coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed work might independently give the same all-rank path-metric retraction formula under metric fixed-point or combinatorial terminology.

The 2021 order-preserving partial-contraction and 2026 narrower-monoid papers were only accessible as abstracts, not complete text; their stated objects and advertised results do not dominate the all-full-contraction theorem.
A later amendment of the 2021 conjecture, if any, was not found; the comparison is only to its published display.

value.rationale: Addresses the explicitly stated open problem of the full-contraction semigroup image-rank distribution for every interior rank in a natural infinite family. Reveals a concrete first counterexample (n=7, image rank 3) to the published Conjecture 14, with a general coefficient formula and a reproducible finite witness. Not a mere reparametrization of the previously known top- and bottom-rank counts.
